statements.status_notes: Netty 4.1.136.Final causes FIPS test timeout (TestFipsEnd2End hangs on index creation). Investigating compatibility issue with FIPS mode before upgrading. The vulnerability affects DNS codec memory leak with malformed DNS packets, but Elasticsearch's typical deployment does not expose DNS codec to untrusted input.

Netty 4.1.136.Final cannot be adopted on Elasticsearch 9.4: jar-swap A/B under FIPS shows HTTPS hangs after a successful TLS handshake (TestFipsEnd2End fails creating an index). Bisect isolated the failure to netty-handler FlowControlHandler changes in 4.1.136 when loaded via the x-pack-security module, which embeds its own Netty jars and a copy of transport-netty4. Elasticsearch 9.4's HTTP pipeline uses FlowControlHandler with auto-read disabled; 8.19 does not and accepts 4.1.136.Final. Keep 9.4 on 4.1.135.Final until an upstream Elasticsearch or Netty fix lands. GHSA-mfg7-5gfp-c4w3 is a DNS codec memory leak with malformed packets; Elasticsearch's typical deployment does not expose the DNS codec to untrusted input.
